body:
Making internal/streaming a separate Go module introduces a transitive dependency issue that is currently breaking the integration tests in CI.

Because Go ignores replace directives in dependencies, when a test application (like openaiclient) imports openai-go, the compiler tries to resolve this internal/streaming module path. Since otelc's syncDeps only adds replace directives for direct leaf modules, internal/streaming is not replaced in the test application's environment, causing the build to fail with a module resolution error.

To fix this without complex replace tracking inside otelc, we should consider keeping the code shared via file copying/generation (e.g. keeping internal/streaming under openai-go and copying it to v2/ and v3/ using a Makefile task or check script).

Is this needed? If the template references return values (e.g. `{{.FuncReturn 0}}`), `funcTemplateData.returns()` already calls `collectReturnValues` which names them before we get here. and if the template doesn't reference returns, the injected code doesn't use return names either, so naming them here does nothing useful.

This same fix was discussed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-compile-instrumentation/pull/799#discussion_r3689788318

I'd suggest dropping this from this PR and doing it properly in a followup. The fix handles signature-level collisions, but doesn't account for global identifiers or locals in the function body. A synthetic name like `_ignoredParam1` could still shadow a package-level variable.

See the issue I opened for this: #1014, we should probably use CRC32 hashes in the identifier names instead to make collisions nearly impossible.

This still performs three environment lookups on every Instrumented call. The cache avoids repeated list parsing, but not the os.Getenv calls. Could the performance claim be narrowed and the benchmark compare base and head for unset and configured-list cases?

If a caller explicitly sends an HTTP request where the method is exactly `"_OTHER"`, `requestMethodAttrs` returns:
- `http.request.method=_OTHER`
- `http.request.method_original=_OTHER`

This violates the OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions for [`http.request.method_original`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.37.0/docs/http/http-spans.md), which explicitly states that it is conditionally required:
> "If and only if it's different than `http.request.method`."

Because `_OTHER` == `_OTHER`, `method_original` must be omitted (i.e., return an empty `attribute.KeyValue{}`) when the raw method is `_OTHER`.
